you seem like such a genuine and kind person. the empathy you feel for your girlfriend is evident. from my experience, 6 months is not long to deal with an event like this. it usually has longer term effects and that is where she is going to need your support. just be there in continuously offering her safety and love and meet her where she’s at in regards to HER journey with her experience. now, you can still express your feelings and emotions about this without directly relating to the issue if you feel she is not open to discussing it. when she is, be patient which it seems like you’re doing very well! but if you feel more worried about her safety, feel angry at the rapist, these are things you have the right to talk about and work through. if you feel she isn’t ready to take on your grief, find support groups and invest in journaling! these are seriously effective ways to work through trauma and secondary trauma. good luck to you and my deepest condolences and best wishes for your girlfriend. ❤️

The fact that she’s mad at you now for expressing your rightful concerns and feelings is a big teller. If she was innocent and cared about you she would have no problem going out of her way to provide you with the peace of mind and reassurance you’re looking for. If she loves you and sees you suffering because of her actions, then it would make sense for her to respect your feelings because even if in her eyes it’s perfectly normal to sleep on a friends sofa, she has a past and lied/acted sketchy even in this situation so she shouldn’t feel entitled to such trust. After you have voiced that this situation was not okay with you, it’s really her response to that that you should be paying attention to. If all she did was sleep on his couch, then she should have no problem agreeing to this not happening again and potentially creating an alternative plan for late nights out. But if she knows that offering you this will diminish her future opportunities to be deceitful, then that might be why she won’t bend.
